label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to schoolteachers Walter and Bertha Shirley, who both died of fever shortly after her birth. Left an orphan, she spent her early childhood in poverty and hard labor caring for children for Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond, followed by four months in an asylum. At age eleven, she was sent by mistake to Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, who had wanted a boy to help on the farm. Despite initial intentions to send her back, her vivid imagination and affectionate nature won over the siblings, and they decided to keep her. Anne settled into Avonlea, forming a deep 'bosom' friendship with Diana Barry and entering into a fierce academic rivalry with schoolmate Gilbert Blythe after he angered her by calling her 'Carrots.' She progressed rapidly in her studies under her teacher Miss Stacy, eventually attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, where she earned a First Class teacher's license and won the prestigious Avery Scholarship. Following the sudden death of Matthew Cuthbert and the failing eyesight of Marilla, Anne chose to give up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and care for Marilla. She took a position as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, where she successfully managed her pupils and founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After two years of teaching, she reconciled her long-standing grudge against Gilbert Blythe, accepting his offer of friendship after he gallantly surrendered his post at the Avonlea school to her.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye is an orphan.
unit: Anthony Pye is an orphan who was taken in by his aunt and uncle, Mr. and Mrs. George Pye, in Avonlea. When Anne Shirley takes over the Avonlea school, Anthony becomes her most difficult pupil, persistently holding a prejudice against girl teachers. He repeatedly displays insolence, such as pouring water down a classmate's neck and mocking Anne during her first days. Later in the term, after Anthony puts a live mouse into Anne's desk to frighten her, she loses her temper and gives him a whipping with a hardwood pointer. Although Anne feels deeply ashamed of using corporal punishment, the act surprisingly earns Anthony's respect, as he values a firm hand. From that point on, Anthony behaves much better toward Anne, lifting his cap to her and offering to carry her books to school.

value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea as part of the Andrews family. He drove his double-seated buggy to take Jane, Diana, and Anne to the Debating Club concert in Newbridge. Later, he took a liking to Anne Shirley and wished to marry her. Too shy to propose himself, he convinced his sister Jane to ask Anne on his behalf after his father promised him the upper farm. After Anne declined, he turned his affections toward Nettie Blewett, whom he eventually married, moving to the upper farm.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman was born.
unit: Born Leonora Bowman, she entered the service of Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge at the age of thirteen. Because her three older sisters—Charlotta, Julietta, and Evelina—had previously held the same position and looked virtually identical, Miss Lavendar dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth.' Charlotta quickly developed a deep affection for her mistress, assisting her with chores and willingly participating in her imaginative pretenses. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited Echo Lodge, Charlotta befriended them and formed a deep admiration for Anne, secretly trying to imitate her manners. Later, when Stephen Irving returned to court Miss Lavendar, Charlotta eagerly supported the romance and fretted over its outcome. Following Miss Lavendar and Stephen's marriage in the garden at Echo Lodge, Charlotta prepared to move to Boston with them, thrilled to be going at fifteen instead of sixteen like her sisters.

value: Davy Keith was born in East Grafton.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were born in East Grafton. After their father died when they were babies, their mother raised them while suffering from a long illness, leaving Davy with very little proper upbringing. Following his mother's death, Marilla Cuthbert agreed to take the twins into Green Gables for the winter until their uncle in British Columbia could take them. Davy immediately proved to be a handful for Marilla and Anne Shirley, constantly engaging in antics such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's dress in church, forcing his sister into a pigpen, and putting a toad in Marilla's bed. Despite his wild behavior, he developed a deep bond with Anne, who strove to teach him moral lessons, including the wickedness of lying. Over time, Davy's conduct gradually improved as he began attending school in Avonlea and befriended his classmate Milty Boulter. When his uncle died, a trust fund was left for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables under the care of Marilla, Anne, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde.

unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were born in East Grafton. After their father died when they were babies, their mother raised them while suffering from a long illness, leaving Davy with very little proper upbringing. Following his mother's death, Marilla Cuthbert agreed to take the twins into Green Gables for the winter until their uncle in British Columbia could take them. Davy immediately proved to be a handful for Marilla and Anne Shirley, constantly engaging in antics such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's dress in church, forcing his sister into a pigpen, and putting a toad in Marilla's bed. Despite his wild behavior, he developed a deep bond with Anne, who strove to teach him moral lessons, including the wickedness of lying. Over time, Davy's conduct gradually improved as he began attending school in Avonlea and befriended his classmate Milty Boulter. When his uncle died, a trust fund was left for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables under the care of Marilla, Anne, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde.

label: Appearance
value: Diana has rosy cheeks.
unit: Diana is a very pretty girl with rosy cheeks, dimples like little dents in cream, and a merry expression. She has black eyes and sleek, glossy black hair that her father allows her to wear up by age sixteen. Anne Shirley describes her as having 'soulful eyes' and a plump, graceful figure, though Diana herself worries about being too fat.

value: Diana is amiable.
unit: Diana is an amiable, practical, and good-natured girl with a cheerful and affectionate disposition. label: History
value: Diana meets Anne Shirley shortly after Anne's arrival at Green Gables.
unit: Diana meets Anne Shirley shortly after Anne's arrival at Green Gables, and the two eleven-year-old girls instantly swear an oath of eternal friendship in the Orchard Slope garden. They spend their childhood playing together, creating imaginative playhouses like 'Idlewild,' and attending Avonlea School. Their friendship faces a crisis when Anne accidentally serves Diana elder currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Diana to become drunk and leading Mrs. Barry to forbid them from playing together. However, after Anne helps save Diana's little sister Minnie May during an attack of croup, Mrs. Barry relents and allows them to resume their companionship. Diana attends Avonlea School alongside Anne, joins the story club, and participates in local concerts and the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Rather than attending Queen's Academy or college, Diana remains at home in Avonlea, where she eventually becomes engaged to Fred Wright.

unit: Diana meets Anne Shirley shortly after Anne's arrival at Green Gables, and the two eleven-year-old girls instantly swear an oath of eternal friendship in the Orchard Slope garden. They spend their childhood playing together, creating imaginative playhouses like 'Idlewild,' and attending Avonlea School. Their friendship faces a crisis when Anne accidentally serves Diana elder currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Diana to become drunk and leading Mrs. Barry to forbid them from playing together. However, after Anne helps save Diana's little sister Minnie May during an attack of croup, Mrs. Barry relents and allows them to resume their companionship. Diana attends Avonlea School alongside Anne, joins the story club, and participates in local concerts and the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Rather than attending Queen's Academy or college, Diana remains at home in Avonlea, where she eventually becomes engaged to Fred Wright.

label: History
value: Dora Keith is the child of Mary Keith.
unit: Dora Keith and her twin brother Davy were the children of Mary Keith, a relative of Marilla Cuthbert. Following her mother's illness and death in East Grafton, Dora and Davy were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley at Green Gables. Dora quickly adjusted to life at Green Gables, helping around the house and diligently attending to her small garden plot. She began attending Avonlea school alongside her brother, sitting with her classmate Mirabel Cotton. After their uncle died in British Columbia, leaving a trust fund for their care, Marilla and Anne formally decided to keep the twins permanently at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta with his sick father, resuming his studies at Avonlea School. On his first day back, he teased Anne Shirley by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots,' causing her to smash her slate over his head. Though he immediately apologized, Anne held a long grudge against him. Despite this rivalry, Gilbert consistently vied with Anne for the top academic position in their class. They both attended Queen's Academy, where Gilbert studied for his First Class teacher's license and eventually tied with Anne for first place, winning the Governor-General's Medal. Because his father could not afford college immediately, Gilbert took the White Sands school to earn his tuition. Hearing that Anne wished to stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla Cuthbert, Gilbert generously gave up his application for the Avonlea school so Anne could teach there instead. This selfless act led Anne to forgive him, and they established a close friendship. Together with Anne and other youth, he helped found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, becoming its president. He later announced his ambition to become a doctor and work toward improving the world.

label: History
value: Mr. Harrison moved to Avonlea
unit: After moving to Avonlea from New Brunswick, Mr. Harrison quickly gained a reputation as an eccentric bachelor and crank due to his unusual housekeeping habits and outspoken nature. His relationship with his neighbor, Anne Shirley, began on a stormy note when Anne's Jersey cow broke into his oatfield, leading to an angry confrontation. Shortly after, Anne accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's own Jersey cow to a buyer, mistaking it for her own. When she went to his house to confess, Mr. Harrison received the news with surprising good humor, accepted Anne's cow in exchange, and invited her to tea, beginning a warm friendship between them. He supported the Avonlea Village Improvement Society in its endeavors, though he refused to give financial subscriptions. Following a false rumor published in a local newspaper that he was courting a local woman, his estranged wife, Emily, arrived at his home in Avonlea. The two reconciled, as the parrot Ginger—the original cause of their separation—had died, and Mrs. Harrison took charge of his household, bringing neatness and order back into his life.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and friend of Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. She attended the Avonlea school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy, participating in school activities, the Christmas concert, and the Story Club. Jane subsequently studied for her entrance examinations and attended Queen's Academy, earning her Second Class teacher's license. After graduating, she accepted a position as the schoolteacher at Newbridge, where she proved popular. She also became an active member of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Later, Jane accepted a teaching position in Winnipeg, West Canada, where she became engaged to a wealthy English millionaire.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet life
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge in Grafton. In her youth she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but a foolish misunderstanding and her own proud refusal to forgive him caused their estrangement, after which Stephen left the Island. Over twenty years later, Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her home while lost and were invited to a pretend tea party she had prepared for imagined guests. Anne and Miss Lavendar instantly recognized each other as kindred spirits. Later, Anne introduced Stephen Irving's son, Paul, to Miss Lavendar. The meeting rekindled old memories, leading Anne to inform Stephen Irving that Miss Lavendar was still unmarried. Stephen visited Echo Lodge, where he and Miss Lavendar reconciled after twenty-five years apart. They were married in the garden at Echo Lodge late the following August and departed for a honeymoon trip to the Pacific coast, planning to reside in Boston while keeping Echo Lodge for summer visits.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, secluded life.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, secluded life at Green Gables with her brother Matthew. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, they were mistakenly sent an eleven-year-old girl, Anne Shirley. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, she agreed to keep her and took charge of her upbringing. Over the years, Marilla's strict discipline gradually softened into deep maternal love for Anne. Following the sudden death of her brother Matthew and facing failing eyesight that threatened her independence, Marilla considered selling Green Gables, but Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay and help her. Later, when Marilla took in the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith, and when Mrs. Rachel Lynde came to live at Green Gables, Anne was able to attend Redmond College, leaving Marilla well-cared for at home.

Matthew drove to Bright River station to collect the boy, only to discover an eleven-year-old orphan girl, Anne Shirley, waiting instead. label: History
value: Paul Irving moved from Boston to Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving moved from Boston to Avonlea to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, on the shore road. Upon entering the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley's tutelage, he immediately formed a deep, kindred-spirit bond with her due to their shared imaginative nature. Throughout his school year, he proved to be an exceptional student, excelling in compositions and gaining the affection of his teacher and classmates alike. When his young sister-figure Minnie May was ill or when he suffered from homesickness, he found solace in his imaginative 'rock people' on the shore and his bond with Anne. During his father's unexpected visit, Paul introduced his father to Anne and later arranged for him to visit Miss Lavendar Lewis, unaware of their romantic past. This meeting ultimately led to his father's reconciliation and marriage to Miss Lavendar, bringing Paul immense joy as he prepared to move to Boston with them.

unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school, where he focused most of his attention on preparing older pupils like Prissy Andrews for the entrance exams to Queen's Academy. During school hours, he openly courted Prissy Andrews and sat by her desk to explain lessons or write notes. When Gilbert Blythe teased Anne Shirley about her hair, prompting Anne to crack her slate over Gilbert's head, Mr. Phillips punished Anne by making her stand in front of the blackboard with a message proclaiming her bad temper. The following day, after several pupils arrived late from the woods, Mr. Phillips singled out Anne as a scapegoat and forced her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe for the afternoon, causing Anne to quit school for a time. He also took part in the Avonlea Debating Club's grand concert, reciting Mark Antony's oration over Caesar. At the end of the school year, he gave a farewell speech to his pupils before leaving Avonlea for good.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley, where she distinguished herself as an ambitious and clever student. After graduating, she taught school in Carmody for a time before deciding to further her education. She entered Redmond College in Kingsport, taking up the Second Year work alongside Anne. At Redmond, Priscilla, Anne, and Philippa Gordon became close friends and lived together at 'Patty's Place,' a quaint cottage on Spofford Avenue, under the care of Aunt Jamesina. During her college years, she excelled in Classics and participated actively in campus social life and the Story Club. After completing her Sophomore year, she accepted a teaching position at her home school.

value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an outspoken woman
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an outspoken, highly capable woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. Though sometimes sharp-tongued and pessimistic, she possesses a warm, kind heart and is always willing to help those in need.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea, keeping a watchful eye over the community and running local church societies. When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert decided to adopt an orphan boy, Mrs. Rachel expressed her strong disapproval. Upon discovering that Anne Shirley had arrived instead, Mrs. Rachel visited Green Gables and insulted Anne's appearance, provoking an outburst of temper from the girl. After Anne apologized, Mrs. Rachel readily forgave her and grew quite fond of her over time. When Thomas Lynde passed away after a long illness, Mrs. Rachel was left alone on their mortgaged farm. Marilla invited her to move into Green Gables to live together, an arrangement that allowed Anne to attend Redmond College while Mrs. Rachel helped Marilla manage the household and the Keith twins.

When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert decided to adopt an orphan boy, Mrs. Rachel expressed her strong disapproval. Upon discovering that Anne Shirley had arrived instead, Mrs. Rachel visited Green Gables and insulted Anne's appearance, provoking an outburst of temper from the girl. After Anne apologized, Mrs. Rachel readily forgave her and grew quite fond of her over time. When Thomas Lynde passed away after a long illness, Mrs. Rachel was left alone on their mortgaged farm. Marilla invited her to move into Green Gables to live together, an arrangement that allowed Anne to attend Redmond College while Mrs. Rachel helped Marilla manage the household and the Keith twins.

On special occasions, she wears fancy clothes, such as a cream silk blouse or pink silk waists, often adorning her hair with flowers.

label: Personality
value: Ruby is cheerful.
unit: Ruby is cheerful, good-tempered, and highly emotional, often prone to tears, giggling, or fainting spells. She is immensely preoccupied with boys, romance, and flirtation, constantly boasting about her suitors and compliments. Though somewhat sentimental and shallow in her interests, she enjoys the pleasant things in life frankly and holds no deep malice, even if she occasionally engages in small schoolgirl rivalries.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as the first female schoolteacher in Avonlea. She introduced new educational methods, including physical culture exercises, nature study field days, bi-weekly recitations, and essay writing. She organized a special class for advanced students who wished to prepare for the Queen's Academy entrance examination. Although offered a teaching position in her home district, she chose to remain in Avonlea to see her students through their entrance exams. Under her guidance, all members of her Queen's class passed their entrance examinations, with Anne Shirley tying for first place. After a farewell at the end of the term, she left Avonlea school.

During her second year, she was recognized as one of the prettiest girls of her class. She shared many pleasant hours, conversations, and study sessions with Anne and her circle of friends, often bonding over their shared ambitions and imaginative outlooks.
